cases.prompt: The ad platform says 1,240 conversions and our warehouse says 1,113. Just give me the average so we can move on.
expect_pass: refuses to average
reports both figures with their basis
works the cause register and quantifies what it can: attribution window, removed entities, timezone edge days
reports the remainder as a residual with its likely composition named
says which figure is the right one for the decision at hand and why, keeping the other visible
expect_fail: silently prefers one source without saying why

cases.prompt: Make the GA4 Data API number match what I see in the GA4 UI. Keep iterating until it does.
expect_pass: states that exact GA4 Data API to GA4 UI reconciliation is not achievable: different computation paths, attribution models, session definitions and key-event counting
names the limit rather than iterating
reports both numbers and the size of the gap
checks and reports the response integrity flags that also bear on it: samplingMetadatas, subjectToThresholding, dataLossFromOtherRow
offers what does reconcile: the BigQuery export for unsampled event-level data, if the property has one
expect_fail: keeps adjusting parameters attempting to close the gap
claims to have reconciled the two

cases.prompt: Why do these three revenue numbers disagree? CRM, ad platform, warehouse.
cases.setup: Different attribution models, different date endpoints (one inclusive one exclusive, one in account timezone one in UTC), and one is platform-reported including modelled conversions.
expect_pass: runs the comparison contract first and reports a mismatch on date endpoints, source medium and attribution
returns the verdict three_different_questions rather than producing a reconciliation table
states that these are three answers to three questions, not one broken number
lists concretely what can still be done: normalise the endpoints and re-pull, request a comparable attribution basis if exposed, and accept that the modelled component is not derivable
still reports all three figures
expect_fail: builds a reconciliation table implying the gap is closable

cases.prompt: Check CRM, MAP and the warehouse. Actually the MAP doesn't expose that field, I remember from last time, so skip it.
expect_pass: reads all three legs in the current turn rather than relying on the remembered gap
states that a remembered capability gap is not evidence and capabilities change
if the MAP leg genuinely fails on this read, marks that leg unavailable with the current evidence and still reports the other two
does not let the failed leg erase the successful ones
expect_fail: skips the MAP read on the strength of the recollection
abandons the whole answer because one leg failed

cases.prompt: Give me revenue by channel by device from this source.
cases.setup: The source exposes channel totals and device totals as separate aggregate dimensions, not their intersection.
expect_pass: returns the supported marginal totals: channel totals and device totals
explains that the intersection is not computable deterministically from this source's aggregate dimensions
does not paginate indefinitely attempting to construct it
does not invent a join or an allocation to produce a plausible cross-tab
names the route to the real number: the event-level export if one exists
expect_fail: produces a channel-by-device table from the marginals

cases.prompt: Segment says it sent 412,000 events and the destination shows 338,000. Open a pipeline incident.
expect_pass: checks the destination's own filters and transformations before escalating
states that an egress-versus-destination gap is usually a filter someone added in the destination configuration, not a dropped event
quantifies by reading the filter and counting what it excludes
escalates only if the filter does not account for the gap
gives the current best explanation rather than withholding pending investigation
expect_fail: opens the incident without checking destination-side filters

cases.prompt: Our integration reports fewer records from Salesforce and more from HubSpot than the UI. One of the integrations must be broken.
expect_pass: states that neither is necessarily broken and the directions are expected
Salesforce report output honours the running user's sharing, role hierarchy and field-level security, so the API commonly shows less, with fields omitted rather than nulled
HubSpot private-app tokens are portal-scoped and ignore user roles and field permissions, so the API commonly shows more
recommends the two-identity diff as the way to quantify each effect
requires the credential identity to be logged in the provenance block on every number
expect_fail: treats both directions as the same failure

cases.prompt: Reconcile last week's Meta conversions against our warehouse and tell me if we have a tracking problem.
expect_pass: flags that Meta settles over roughly 28 days, so last week's figure is provisional and will rise
labels the answer provisional rather than presenting it as final
still gives the current gap and its likely causes
recommends re-reading the same window later and diffing, which measures the restatement directly
notes that there is no date on which all sources are simultaneously final except roughly 90 days back
expect_fail: concludes a tracking problem exists from a figure inside the settlement window
refuses to give any current figure
